title: Shared Library Database Entities (Monolithic Entity Library)
pattern: Multiple independent services compile against a single shared custom library containing all database table entity structures and schema definitions.
why_bad: Any schema modification (e.g., Service C adds `billing_address`) forces a version update of the shared library, requiring a complete rebuild and redeployment of unrelated services (Service A, which does not care about billing).
detection: An external shared library containing database-mapping models imported by multiple distinct service projects.
counterexample: Shared data-transfer libraries containing strictly defined, versioned API protocol schemas (like Protobuf types) that are designed for wire transfer compatibility.
source: Mark Richards & Neal Ford, *Fundamentals of Software Architecture* (2020), Chapter 13 ("Database Partitioning").
